newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea business group sees slow outlook in July.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea business group sees slow outlook in July.

text.p: South Korean businesses expect the economy to remain depressed in July, but sentiment has improved from June and a from a year ago, a corporate survey by the Federation of Korean Industries (FKI) said on Wednesday.

The Business Survey Index (BSI) provided by the FKI, a powerful lobby group representing the nation's biggest conglomerates, or chaebols, stood at 87 for July against 77 for the same month a year earlier and 80 for June this year.
A BSI figure higher than 100 means businesses' outlook is bullish. Anything less than 100 means their outlook is bearish.
The federation cited a continued slowdown in private consumption and investment for the expected downturn.
However, exports were likely to pick up on the easing of the Japanese yen's fall against the dollar and the recovery in international prices of major export items.

It said corporate consumption was likely to flag due to a decline in the number of working days as workers take their summer holidays in July. Companies also have less to spend as they tighten their budgets.
The BSI for consumption was 92 for July, unchanged from June. It stood at 86 a year before.
The exports outlook turned slightly bullish on the back of a possible continued easing of the Japanese yen's fall and the central bank's efforts to stabilise the Korean won versus the dollar.
The BSI for exports was 102 for July, compared with 89 a year ago and 100 for June.
However, corporate liquidity conditions are forecast to stay tight in July as financial institutions toughen their credit screening.
Deteriorating sales and profitability are also expected to aggravate companies' internal funding, it said.
The BSI for corporate financial status was 94 for July versus 93 a year before and 92 for June.
The survey, which covered 600 companies, had a response rate of 90.7 percent.
